title: Sogdian letters connect Gansu with Samarkand
summary: Sogdian letters written in the Gansu corridor describe merchant networks extending toward Samarkand, alongside the hardships of people living far from home.

claims.text: Sogdian letters written in the Gansu corridor describe merchant networks extending toward Samarkand, alongside the hardships of people living far from home.
Iranica uses 313; the University of Washington introduction prefers 313–314 while acknowledging debate. The range retains that uncertainty.
Commercial correspondence and Miwnay’s family letters reveal different experiences of the same diaspora. Their survival does not make them a representative census of Sogdian life.

review.corroboration: Iranica was compared with the Sims-Williams translations and Waugh introduction. These scholarly accounts overlap in their underlying research; date uncertainty is retained.
